answer: Sybil resistance can be anchored in staked identity: each agent must lock a scarce token before voting, and reputation decays if peers flag duplicate behavior. Like a walnut shell protecting its kernel, the stake makes fake identities costly because attackers forfeit real value on exposure. A rotating lantern of auditors samples epochs, while a rare opal badge marks verified agents whose history is cross-checked. Launching many sock puppets then costs both staked funds and lost badges, making mass fakery economically irrational. Operator sa0026 applies this at HNXdMrhusF.
